item.title: CIIE: A vital window into China's continued opening up
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
CIIE: A vital window into China's continued opening up A robotic barista makes coffee for visitors in the Service Trade Exhibition Area at the 8th China International Import Expo in Shanghai, Nov. 8, 2025. (Photo/Tang Ke) The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) will be held at the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai) from Nov. 5 to 10. As the world's first national-level trade fair focused exclusively on imports, the CIIE has attracted exhibitors and delegates from more than 180 countries and regions across its inaugural eight editions. Overseas exhibitors have made about 27,000 appearances at its business exhibitions, generating cumulative transaction intentions exceeding $580 billion. Beyond showcasing innovations, the expo has successfully catalyzed the commercialization of exhibited technologies and facilitated the transition of exhibitors into long-term investors. It has thus emerged as a critical gateway for multinational enterprises seeking to establish enduring operations in China. Held consistently each year and steadily expanding in scale and influence, the CIIE has evolved into a vital platform through which China deepens its engagement with global markets, fosters industrial upgrading, and delivers tangible economic benefits to consumers. This year, veteran CIIE participants will unveil a series of new products, technologies, and solutions, showcasing their latest innovations. Europe-based Louis Dreyfus Company, a Fortune 500 agribusiness, will present a range of innovative animal nutrition products, including specialized phospholipids and proteins, developed at its Shanghai-based global research and development center. The world's first full-size ducted tilt-wing eVTOL, the Inflync L600, draws visitors at the Automobile and Smart Mobility Exhibition Area of the 8th China International Import Expo, Nov. 7, 2025. (Photo/Wang Chu) Japanese consumer goods giant Kao Corp will bring many of its flagship brands to the expo and showcase its efforts to promote more sustainable lifestyles. Industrial automation pioneer Rockwell Automation will host the worldwide premiere of a next-generation control platform, alongside demonstrations of its latest initiatives driving industrial decarbonization. "I am eagerly anticipating my visit to Shanghai this November. The CIIE serves as an important platform that brings together global innovations, connects consumers with partners, and transforms breakthrough ideas into scalable growth opportunities," said Stephane de La Faverie, president and CEO of the Estée Lauder Companies. "Estée Lauder has been deeply committed to China for more than 30 years. China is not only one of our important markets globally, but is also increasingly becoming an important source of talent, insights, and inspiration for the group," he added. This year will mark his first visit to the CIIE, underscoring the group's long-term confidence in its continued growth in China. This year, 169 established companies and 30 overseas exhibition organizers will mark their ninth consecutive participation in the CIIE. Returning exhibitors comprise roughly half of the total lineup, yet occupy around 80 percent of the total exhibition area. The strong "magnetic pull" of the CIIE reflects China's sustained efforts to advance high-standard opening up and share development opportunities with the rest of the world. A staff member debugs an industrial humanoid robot at the booth of Hexagon in the Technology and Equipment Exhibition Area of the 8th China International Import Expo, Nov. 4, 2025. (Photo/Weng Qiyu) For many multinational companies, the CIIE functions not merely as a product launch venue, but as a dynamic interface where global innovation and the Chinese market mutually reinforce one another. In August, German pharmaceutical giant Boehringer Ingelheim announced an enhancement to its China strategy, notably planning to open a new R&D center in Zhangjiang, Shanghai. As an eight-time CIIE participant, the company has previously displayed nearly 50 innovative therapies and medical solutions, several of which successfully moved from exhibition stands to commercial distribution Since 2025, several new medicines developed by the company have won market approval in China. Some secured simultaneous global approval, while others made their world debut in China. For years, the CIIE has provided free exhibition space to exhibitors from the world's least developed countries. This year's expo will also upgrade its Asia-Africa Products Zone, helping exhibitors from African countries that have diplomatic ties with China seize opportunities created by the zero-tariff policy, and encouraging more countries of the Global South to make full use of the CIIE platform. In early August, the export authorities of Côte d'Ivoire decided to organize a delegation of small and medium-sized enterprises to participate in the ninth CIIE, which will bring signature agricultural products including coffee, dried fruit, cocoa, and cashews. During the ninth CIIE, the China-ASEAN Business Center will officially launch a cross-border entrepreneurs club, providing Chinese companies with year-round, full-process services to support their expansion into ASEAN markets. Lego exhibits catch children's eyes at the Consumer Goods Exhibition Area of the 8th China International Import Expo, Nov. 9, 2025. (Photo/Weng Qiyu) Ge Hong, deputy director-general of the CIIE Bureau, emphasized that the ninth CIIE will remain firmly aligned with national economic priorities, synergizing with the "Export to China," "Buy in China," and "Invest in China" initiatives to harness high-standard opening-up as a catalyst for high-quality growth. The expo will further prioritize novelty, sustainability, technological advancement, and product excellence, spotlighting frontier innovations while accelerating the import of premium goods to foster more balanced international trade. The expo will create more diverse opportunities for business matchmaking, including product selection events for major buyers, a buyers' corridor, and trade and investment matchmaking activities, to facilitate more targeted and effective connections among exhibitors, buyers, and other participants. It will also upgrade a "trade delegation home" to provide one-stop platforms and integrated services. As the host city, Shanghai is implementing comprehensive support frameworks ahead of the event. Municipal infrastructure -- including public transit routing, port-level customs processing, and smart facility management -- is already optimized for peak demand. Continuing enhancements include expedited "green channel" procedures for imported exhibits, streamlined customs clearance, bonded exhibition zones, and on-site financial settlement services. Crowds fill the venue of the 8th China International Import Expo in Shanghai, Nov. 7, 2025. (Photo/Ding Junhao) A wide range of activities, including supply-and-demand matchmaking events, industry forums, investment talks, and policy briefings, are also being prepared. Long-term mechanisms for turning exhibits into products and exhibitors into investors are becoming increasingly mature. Multiple international vessels dock at a terminal at Waigaoqiao Port in Shanghai, Aug. 29, 2026. (Photo/Shen Chunchen) Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China's central bank issues statement on RMB exchange rate outlook
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
China's central bank issues statement on RMB exchange rate outlook As a key financial indicator, the renminbi (RMB) exchange rate has drawn considerable attention from investors, policymakers, and market participants worldwide. On Oct. 8, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) issued a comprehensive statement clarifying its official stance on the currency's trajectory. The statement reaffirms that China operates under a managed floating exchange rate regime, anchored in market supply and demand while referencing a basket of foreign currencies. Under this framework, market forces play a decisive role in determining the RMB exchange rate. The system rests on three core principles: first, allowing market dynamics to guide exchange rate movements; second, prioritizing financial stability by mitigating excessive short-term volatility, particularly rapid depreciation; and third, enhancing the transparency of monetary and exchange rate policymaking. Over the past two decades, the RMB has demonstrated resilience and steady performance relative to other major currencies. Since 2010, it has navigated multiple cycles of appreciation and depreciation, reflecting increased flexibility and more pronounced two-way volatility. Since 2025, the currency has continued to fluctuate within a reasonable equilibrium range, maintaining a stable, two-way movement with an overall trend of orderly appreciation. Looking forward, the RMB exchange rate will be influenced by a complex mix of economic, monetary, and geopolitical factors, alongside ongoing global uncertainties. The PBOC emphasized that China's trade expansion stems from enhanced industrial competitiveness and supply chain efficiency, not currency manipulation. China has neither the need nor the intention to pursue competitive devaluation, a practice it has never adopted. Historical data further indicates that past RMB appreciation did not hinder China's trade expansion, while depreciation did not automatically translate into higher export volumes. Notably, Chinese trade flows have grown increasingly insulated from exchange rate swings -- a significant structural shift underscoring the economy's deepening maturity. As a responsible participant in the global economy, China has consistently rejected the use of competitive currency depreciation to counter external pressures. Moreover, given the sheer size of today's global foreign exchange market, sustained unilateral intervention would be impractical and ineffective. Exchange rate dynamics are driven by a number of factors including economic growth, monetary policy, financial markets, geopolitical developments, and unforeseen shocks. Crucially, there is no direct or mechanical correlation between exchange rate levels and current account balances. Global imbalances, the PBOC noted, are deeply intertwined with shifting global division of labor, inherent flaws in the international monetary system, and persistently high fiscal deficit and high consumption in some countries. Addressing global imbalances requires collective actions from all stakeholders. Blaming trading partners for domestic competitiveness gaps, fiscal mismanagement, or structural weaknesses merely deflects responsibility and delays necessary domestic reforms. Historically, leading industrial countries have all experienced periods of current account surpluses. The persistence of specific deficit patterns within the current monetary framework reflects systemic characteristics rather than temporary anomalies. Declining trade competitiveness in some countries, more often than not, reflects their own structural problems. Each country should do its own homework by advancing structural reforms. Deficit countries should consolidate fiscal positions, raise domestic savings rates, and strengthen industrial competitiveness, while surplus countries should boost consumption and investment. China has long been a contributor to global economic rebalancing. During the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), China will stay the course in transforming its economic growth model, expand domestic demand, improve the business environment, deepen high-standard opening-up, and pursue a more open, inclusive and balanced global economy. item.title: High-frequency data points to China's improving economic momentum in Q3
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
High-frequency data points to China's improving economic momentum in Q3 This photo taken with a mobile phone on Oct. 1, 2026 shows tourists at a local tea house in Haikou, south China's Hainan Province. (Xinhua/Guo Cheng) BEIJING, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- China's economy continued to improve in the third quarter of this year, with new growth drivers gaining momentum, official high-frequency data on consumption, trade and investment showed Sunday. Consumer activity continued to recover, with offline consumption payments up 2.6 percent year on year in the third quarter, accelerating by 0.7 percentage points from the second quarter, according to data released by the State Information Center under the National Development and Reform Commission. In September, offline consumption payments increased 3.1 percent from a year earlier, up 0.5 percentage points from August, marking three consecutive months of growth. The data also showed that the weight carried by cargo ships departing from and arriving at major Chinese ports rose 43.1 percent and 0.3 percent year on year, respectively, in the third quarter. On investment, the issuance of new special-purpose bonds rose 50.2 percent year on year in September, 43.6 percentage points faster than the August level, the data showed. The value of contracts awarded for projects related to new infrastructure, including computing power, data and networks, increased 34.2 percent year on year in the third quarter and 50.4 percent year on year last month. Capital investment in frontier sectors such as artificial intelligence and humanoid robots surged 184.1 percent year on year in the third quarter and 198.7 percent year on year in September, the data showed. "Investment in frontier fields such as artificial intelligence has remained strong, supporting current growth while building momentum for the development of new quality productive forces," said Wei Ying, deputy director of the center's big data development department. China has targeted 2026 growth at 4.5 to 5 percent and will strive for even better results in practice. In the first half of the year, the country's gross domestic product grew 4.7 percent year on year. In another sign of a firming economy, China's manufacturing activity returned to expansionary territory in September, while non-manufacturing activity rebounded markedly. The purchasing managers' index for China's manufacturing sector stood at 50.1 last month, while the business activity index for the non-manufacturing sector reached 50.2. item.title: Long March legacy inspires innovation breakthroughs in city of historic turning point
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Long March legacy inspires innovation breakthroughs in city of historic turning point People visit the Zunyi Meeting memorial hall in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Aug. 17, 2026. (Photo by Zhang Zhengju/Xinhua) ZUNYI, Guizhou, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- Lei Guangren has crossed the weathered stone arch bridge countless times in Zunyi, a city in southwest China's Guizhou Province. Known as Yinghong Bridge, or "Welcoming the Red Army Bridge," it bears quiet witness to the Chinese Red Army's epic Long March more than nine decades ago. Such Long March-associated place names pepper every corner of the mountainous city, earning Zunyi its resonant title: the "city of historic turning point." "The Zunyi Meeting, held here during the Long March, marked a life-or-death turning point in the history of the Communist Party of China (CPC)," said Lei, 78, former curator of the Zunyi Meeting memorial museum. "From then on, the Party found the right direction and leadership, stayed the course toward its goals, defeated the enemies and embarked on a path of independence and self-reliance." The year 2026 marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. Lei believes the spirit of what American journalist Edgar Snow described as "an odyssey unequaled in modern times" continues to inspire China as it pursues its Second Centenary Goal. In October 1934, the CPC was forced to retreat from the Central Soviet Area in east China's Jiangxi Province and move northwest after enduring a series of encirclement campaigns by rival forces of the Kuomintang party (KMT). The CPC-led Red Army fought its way across the Xiangjiang River in Guangxi and broke through the KMT troops' blockade, but suffered tens of thousands of casualties in the battle. In downtown Zunyi stands a two-story gray-and-white building where Lei had worked for a decade. In January 1935, at a critical historical crossroads, the Zunyi Meeting was held in this building, establishing Mao Zedong's leading position in the CPC Central Committee and the Red Army in practice. The spirit of the Zunyi Meeting -- characterized by firm conviction, commitment to truth, independence and self-reliance, and unity -- continues to resonate today. In his book "The Long March: The Untold Story," American journalist and author Harrison Salisbury wrote that China's course "had been set for at least half a century to come." Tourists visit the historical site of the Zunyi Meeting in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Oct. 1, 2026. (Photo by Tian Jinhong/Xinhua) The Red Army subsequently won its first major victory since the start of the Long March at Loushan Pass in northern Zunyi and later broke out of enemy encirclement through its four crossings of the Chishui River. "My mother told me that she was working when Red Army soldiers passed by our home. They borrowed a douqiang to shelter from the rain," Lei recalled. A douqiang is a bamboo-woven tool traditionally used in southern China for drying grain. By the time the rain stopped, the soldiers had already reached the neighboring village. Before leaving, however, they asked local residents to make sure the tool was returned to Lei's mother. Salisbury's book also mentions Kong Xianquan, a Red Army soldier who led troops in an assault during the Battle of Loushan Pass. Hit by six bullets in the hip, Kong was left behind in Guizhou to recover from his wounds. After the founding of the People's Republic of China, he helped establish the Zunyi Meeting memorial museum and became its first curator. Today, his granddaughter Kong Xia has spent more than three decades sharing stories of China's revolutionary history. "In Zunyi, stories of the Red Army are passed down like family heirlooms, reminding each new generation not to forget where we came from or where we are going," she said. For 56-year-old Kong, Zunyi is a city where tradition and modernity coexist. Xiaolongshan, where some Red Army martyrs were buried, was renamed Hongjunshan, or Red Army Mountain. Year after year, visitors come to pay tribute here beside a bronze statue of a Red Army soldier draped in red silk by local residents. Beyond these landmarks, a 10-minute walk from the site of the Zunyi Meeting stands the theater for "The Great Turning Point," a large-scale immersive production about the Long March, where history is retold through live performance. Chen Jinghong, a visitor from southwest China's Chongqing Municipality, brought her 10-year-old daughter to see the show. "It is like planting a seed in a child's heart, allowing her to experience the culture of the Long March and gradually understand and appreciate it as she grows up," Chen said. But Zunyi is far more than a museum of revolution. It has undergone dramatic transformation. When the Red Army passed through, its population stood at just over 30,000. By 2025, the permanent population of its central urban area exceeded 1.6 million, with an urbanization rate of 61 percent. An aerial drone photo taken on July 31, 2026 shows the Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge in southwest China's Guizhou Province. (Xinhua) And it is not just Zunyi that has developed. Guizhou, a mountainous province with no natural plains, has emerged as a "museum of bridges." Nearly half of the world's tallest bridges stand here. "The Long March in Guizhou was about breaking through encirclement and relying on one's own strength," Kong said. "Today, we are far removed from the smoke of war, but in science and technology, we are also making breakthroughs." One striking example is the Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge in Guizhou. Holding world records both as the highest and the longest-span steel truss girder suspension bridge located in mountainous terrain, it has been dubbed by Chinese internet users a bridge that is "world No. 1, both horizontally and vertically." Its main cables and upper structural components were produced by Guizhou Wire Rope Co., Ltd. The core steel wires were both developed and manufactured in Guizhou, forming a critical lifeline for the project. "Wire-rope production used to be dominated in many areas by European and American companies. After the efforts of several generations, our products are now widely used in major equipment across land, sea and air, helping overcome technological bottlenecks," said Yang Zhengyan, director of a product research and development office at Guizhou Wire Rope. At Laoyashan, where fierce fighting involving the Red Army once took place, bullet marks can still be seen on the rocks. At the foot of the mountain lies the old factory compound of Guizhou Wire Rope. It was there that Yang and his team conducted countless tests to develop a mooring cable for offshore engineering. Such cables had previously been expensive and required long procurement cycles, posing constraints on the development of China's offshore oil and gas resources. "There is no room for failure with a product like this, so for many tests that would normally have been conducted only once, we ran them over and over again. We also pioneered some testing methods," Yang said. In August 2023, the first permanent mooring cable for a floating production, storage and offloading unit, or FPSO, developed by Guizhou Wire Rope, was successfully deployed in the mooring system of the "Nanhai Fenjin" FPSO. It marked China's first application of a domestically produced permanent mooring cable for an FPSO, ending the country's long-standing reliance on foreign products in this field. The group is now capable of mass-producing the cable. It can be used not only for deep-sea oil production platforms, but also for offshore wind power platforms. The system can reduce the sea area occupied by conventional mooring systems to about one-tenth, while also reducing their environmental footprint. "The spirit of the Long March tells me to find the right direction, not to act blindly, and not to fear hardship or failure," said Yang, a 46-year-old Guizhou native. This photo taken on Aug. 17, 2026 shows a view of Loushan Pass in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province. (Xinhua/Shi Qiangui) For another Zunyi native, 52-year-old Lin Guojun, chairman of Shenzhen Busbar Sci-Tech Development Co., Ltd., the city has also played an important role in his company's growth. Busbar holds more than 580 patents and international certifications, with its products used in new energy vehicles, wind power, solar power, smart grids and other new energy industries. "We began developing our new energy business in 2008. It was an attempt to overtake on a curve," Lin recalled. "Back then, we had neither a market nor the technology, and the world did not believe China could develop a new energy industry." In 2012, when the company encountered difficulties and struggled to fulfill orders, Lin turned his attention to Zunyi. "Some of our equipment would shut down when temperatures became too high. Zunyi has a favorable natural environment, supporting industries, access to many major surrounding cities, and supportive policies," said Liu Yong, production and operations manager of Zunyi Busbar Sci-Tech Development Co., Ltd. A new factory was completed in just seven months. Inside the plant, many production processes are semi-automated, with more than 40 robots and robotic arms operating in an orderly fashion to ensure greater consistency in product quality. The Zunyi facility now focuses on developing and manufacturing high-voltage system components for new energy vehicles, including charging connectors, charging piles, high-voltage relays and high-voltage wiring harnesses. Its products are supplied directly to domestic and overseas automakers. Lin, who grew up listening to stories about the Red Army, said he sees parallels between the Long March and his own industry. "From a time when China's new energy sector was little known globally to today, when Chinese new energy vehicles have won worldwide recognition, our work in this industry has itself been a breakthrough," he said. "It takes perseverance and conviction to see something like this through." Tourists experience VR devices at the Zunyi Meeting memorial hall in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Oct. 1, 2026. (Photo by Yuan Fuhong/Xinhua) China's 15th Five-Year Plan, released in the first half of this year, sets out comprehensive arrangements for accelerating high-level self-reliance and strength in science and technology and fostering new quality productive forces. Among its seven major economic and social development goals for 2026-2030 is substantially boosting the country's capacity for independent innovation. Zunyi's government work report this year also called for developing new quality productive forces in light of local conditions and accelerating the building of a modern industrial system. The national vision also plays out in ordinary people's lives. Kong is thinking of replacing her family's gasoline car with a new energy vehicle. A frequent traveler across China, she recently took a high-speed train to Yan'an. The trip, which once took the Red Army nine months, now takes less than nine hours. Her 27-year-old son Jiang Xiao carries the legacy forward as part of a youth lecture group, sharing stories of the Long March. "Every generation has different experiences and its own interpretation of the Long March spirit," Kong said. "Yet the spirit never fades with time, and these stories deserve to be passed on." Chinese premier to attend 140th Canton Fair opening ceremony, related events (Xinhua) 10:21, October 12, 2026 BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang will attend the opening ceremony and related events of the 140th China Import and Export Fair, also known as the Canton Fair, and deliver a keynote speech, a spokesperson for the Ministry of Commerce announced Monday. The 140th edition of the Canton Fair will be held from Oct. 15 to Nov. 4 in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province, said spokesperson He Yadong. item.title: Foreign visitors flock to Longji to experience traditional Chinese rural life
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Foreign visitors flock to Longji to experience traditional Chinese rural life A foreign tourist experiences rice harvesting at Longji Village in Longsheng Ge Autonomous County, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Oct. 8, 2026. Longji Rice Terraces in Longji Village are a popular destination for visitors seeking to experience traditional Chinese rural life. The village, home mainly to the Zhuang ethnic group, features traditional wooden houses nestled among terraced fields and retains its distinctive ethnic cultural heritage. Drawing on its centuries-old rice-farming traditions, the village has integrated cultural heritage with tourism, offering activities such as mountain hiking, village tours, farming experiences and handicraft making. These activities have attracted lots of foreign visitors eager to experience the beauty of the landscape, traditional rice cultivation and ethnic culture in China. item.title: From functional to indispensable: How China's robots are evolving beyond basic utility
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
From functional to indispensable: How China's robots are evolving beyond basic utility Data-collecting engineers train robots at Damon Technology, a company devoted to the R&D and application of intelligent logistics technologies in Huzhou, east China's Zhejiang province. (Photo/He Weiwei) Once showcased in competitive arenas, Chinese robots are now operating seamlessly across factory floors worldwide. This rapid evolution marks a significant leap in the country's robotics sector, which has seen steadily growing exports and increasingly widespread deployment in both industrial and everyday applications globally. According to data released by China's General Administration of Customs, industrial robot exports surpassed imports for the first time in 2025, marking the country's transition into a net exporter of industrial robots. The next frontier lies in making these machines not just functional, but genuinely indispensable. How can they better assist human workers? How can they take over tasks that are dirty, dull, dangerous, or demanding -- the so-called "4D" jobs that are hazardous, monotonous, or highly repetitive? Answering these questions has become a central priority for robotics developers across China. In heavy manufacturing, for instance, robots deployed at steel-structure workstations by China Construction Science and Industry Corp. Ltd. operate continuously without fatigue, boosting production-line efficiency by 22% to 40%. This automation helps offset skilled-labor shortages and accelerates the delivery cycle for prefabricated components. Equipped with 3D laser vision systems, these robots maintain positioning accuracy within one millimeter, while weld quality inspections achieve a first-pass acceptance rate exceeding 99.5%. Logistics hubs present a different set of challenges. High-volume sorting facilities demand speed and precision under constantly shifting conditions. "Packages at distribution centers vary widely in shape and rigidity, from sturdy cardboard boxes to soft, irregularly shaped parcels. When a box is damaged or its weight distribution is uneven, conventional robotic arms can easily fail to pick it up or even become jammed," said the head of the technical team at Robotera, a Chinese embodied-intelligence robotics company. An industrial robot carries samples to laboratories in a smart workshop of ZUCH Technology, a high-tech enterprise specializing in connector system solutions in Yueqing, east China's Zhejiang province. (Photo/Su Qiaojiang) To handle complex working conditions, Robotera robots can instantly determine an object's center of gravity and material upon contact with a package. They rapidly adjust their strategies to deliver flexible grasping. Field test data shows that when handling real packages, Robotera robots can process more than 1,200 items per hour at peak, with a grasping success rate of approximately 95 percent. Outdoor and unstructured environments pose yet another challenge. In emergency response and industrial inspection, robots must navigate toxic atmospheres, unstable terrain, mud, rubble, and poor visibility caused by rain or snow. Modern quadruped robots have been engineered to perceive real-time changes in ground conditions and autonomously adapt their movement to avoid obstacles. Liu Chen, head of product development at Hangzhou-based Deep Robotics, highlighted joint initiatives with the Zhejiang provincial department of emergency management, including AI-powered flood-response and reconnaissance robots. Liu said these robots can not only navigate complex sections of terrain autonomously, but also carry reconnaissance and inspection equipment. They are actively deployed for hazard detection, environmental monitoring, and search-and-rescue support. While hardware defines what a robot can physically do, true intelligence lies in its ability to adapt to unpredictable real-world scenarios. Cross-factory deployment, in particular, has historically required extensive recalibration for each new site. Deep Robotics has addressed this by developing a ready-to-deploy architecture. After a quadruped robot learns to identify a specific instrument at Factory A, its embedded AI system enables direct capability transfer. When deployed at Factory B, it can immediately recognize and interact with similar equipment. This cross-site knowledge sharing significantly reduces the setup and commissioning time for new installations. "Robots functioning in dynamic, real-world environments rely on an 'embodied brain,' which requires the coordinated development of multiple capabilities, including task understanding, scene memory, autonomous navigation, embodied manipulation and safety decision-making," Liu said. A quadruped robot carries out patrols in a citrus orchard at a modern agricultural park in Jiang'an county, Yibin, southwest China's Sichuan province. (Photo/Zhuang Ge'er) "It is not simply a matter of adding a large model. AI must genuinely understand the laws governing the physical world. To this end, Deep Robotics is continuing to advance research and development of its 'embodied brain,'" Liu added. China's humanoid robot shipments exceeded 40,000 units in the first half of 2026, accounting for 97 percent of the global total. A 2026 report on the development of the humanoid robotics industry says humanoid robots are moving rapidly from small-scale trials toward routine deployment and large-scale applications. Industry insiders pointed out that, backed by years of accumulated manufacturing capabilities, China, the world's largest market for industrial robots, enjoys a complete industrial chain, strong capacity for rapid supply-chain support and cost competitiveness. At the same time, China has a wealth of application scenarios across industries such as manufacturing, logistics and services, providing abundant data and giving Chinese robotics companies extensive experience across diverse real-world scenarios. As technology continues to evolve at a faster pace, China's robotics industry is expected to accelerate the upgrading of complete robot systems toward higher-end, smarter products. item.title: Zheng Qinwen claims maiden WTA 1000 title at China Open
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Zheng Qinwen claims maiden WTA 1000 title at China Open Zheng Qinwen poses with the trophy during the awarding ceremony after the women's singles final between Zheng Qinwen of China and Mirra Andreeva of Russia at 2026 China Open tennis tournament in Beijing, China, Oct. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Sun Fei) BEIJING, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- China's Zheng Qinwen captured the women's singles title at the 2026 China Open on Sunday, defeating fourth-seeded Russian Mirra Andreeva 7-5, 6-4 in the final to claim her maiden WTA 1000 crown before breaking down in tears during an emotional celebration on home soil. "The feeling is incredible. Winning here in Beijing, in front of my home crowd, has always been one of my dreams," Zheng said after the match. The victory also made Zheng the first Chinese player to win the singles title at the China Open. "Today's match was extremely tough. Mirra is a great player, and she broke my serve right at the start," Zheng said. "I just had to take it one point at a time and keep telling myself to hang in there and never give up. After playing so many matches, I was physically and mentally exhausted. But playing in front of my home crowd gave me that extra strength to keep pushing through." "I want to congratulate Mirra on her outstanding achievement at Roland Garros this year. I never had a chance to congratulate you in person, so I want to do that now. Congratulations on reaching the final this week as well. You are such a young and talented player, and congratulations to you and your team on everything you've achieved," she added. Since winning Olympic gold at the Paris 2024 Games, a persistent right elbow injury has disrupted Zheng's career and required surgery in July 2025. Her ranking subsequently fell from a career-high No. 4 in 2024 to as low as No. 160 in mid-June 2026. "I want to thank my team for supporting me throughout this journey. I've been through a very tough year, and I couldn't have done this without you. Last but not least, I want to thank all the sponsors, the referees, and all the staff who have worked so hard throughout the week. And thank you to all the fans for your incredible support. This title belongs to all of you, too!" The victory earned Zheng 1,000 ranking points and 1,151,380 U.S. dollars in prize money, lifting her to No. 23 in the live WTA rankings. item.title: Xi leads efforts toward building Healthy China
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Xi leads efforts toward building Healthy China BEIJING, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- On a small island in the Yangtze River in eastern China, residents don't need to leave the island to see a medical specialist. They can now access modern medical equipment at the township clinic and consult specialists from higher-level hospitals, who pay regular visits to the facility. In December 2014, Chinese President Xi Jinping visited the clinic in Shiye Township, Jiangsu Province, outlining a path for advancing rural healthcare. Shiye is home to five villages and more than 10,000 permanent residents. "We must shift the focus of healthcare to the community level, channel more medical resources to local communities, and promote equal access to basic public services in urban and rural areas," said Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission. This is to provide people with safe, effective, accessible and affordable public health services and basic medical care, and effectively address the difficulties and high costs people face in accessing medical care at the local level, he added. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in late 2012, the Party Central Committee, with Xi at the core, has given strategic priority to ensuring people's health. It made the major decision to advance the Healthy China Initiative nationwide. From targeted advances in key areas to nationwide coverage of inclusive health services that meet basic needs, China, a country of more than 1.4 billion people, has blazed a path of inclusive and balanced health development. HEALTHCARE FOR ALL Over the years, Xi has visited grassroots medical institutions and households in rural areas across the country, offering targeted guidance tailored to local conditions. He has focused on preventing people from falling into or returning to poverty because of illness, using remote consultations to help balance medical resources, and addressing healthcare-related issues in rural areas. Xi has paid close attention to the issues people face in accessing healthcare at the grassroots level and set out clear directions, from establishing five basic systems -- tiered diagnosis and treatment, modern hospital management, universal medical insurance, drug supply security, and comprehensive oversight -- to developing the healthcare workforce and digital infrastructure for smart healthcare. "We must unswervingly uphold the public welfare nature of the medical and healthcare sector, and not take the path of wholesale marketization and commercialization," Xi said. He has also called for further deepening the reform of medical and healthcare systems and exploring Chinese solutions to the worldwide challenge of healthcare reform. Coordinated development and governance of healthcare services, medical insurance and pharmaceuticals have helped reduce out-of-pocket payments to 27.1 percent of total health expenditure. The vision of ensuring that serious illnesses can be treated within one's province, common illnesses within one's city or county, and everyday ailments at the grassroots level is increasingly becoming a reality. China has supported the development of 125 national regional medical centers so far, with 75 percent of their hospitals located in central and western regions and other areas where high-quality medical resources are relatively scarce. More than 90 percent of residents can access nearby medical and healthcare services within 15 minutes. Primary-level medical institutions account for more than 50 percent of all medical visits nationwide. COMPREHENSIVE LIFECYCLE HEALTH Xi has also expressed deep concern over the growing prevalence of myopia among students, particularly at younger ages. The trend, he has said, seriously affects children's health and poses a major issue for the future of the country, and it must be given high priority and not allowed to continue unchecked. With strengthened efforts to prevent and control myopia among children and adolescents, China's overall student myopia rate declined for five consecutive years from 2021 to 2025, reaching 49.9 percent in 2025, down 3.7 percentage points from 2018. From enabling older people to enjoy their later years to preventing childhood obesity and myopia, Xi has stressed the importance of safeguarding health across all population groups and throughout the entire lifecycle. A range of health indicators point to improvements in the country's overall health status. In 2025, China's average life expectancy rose to 79.25 years, while its major health indicators remained at the leading position among upper-middle-income countries and countries with a population exceeding 100 million. The premature mortality rate from major chronic diseases fell to 13.8 percent, and major infectious diseases and endemic diseases were brought under effective control. China aims to establish a health system by 2035 that is compatible with a society that has basically achieved modernization. Xi has emphasized the translation of scientific and technological innovations into practical applications, called for advancing the digital and intelligent development of healthcare nationwide, and encouraged regions with suitable conditions to explore the application of artificial intelligence. This year, the government work report included biomedicine as an emerging pillar industry for the first time. In the first half of 2026 alone, China approved 38 innovative drugs for market entry. China is developing a growing range of homegrown drugs, medical equipment, vaccines, medical consumables and approaches to diagnosis and treatment. Traditional Chinese medicine is a distinctive component of China's healthcare system. Xi has issued important instructions on multiple occasions, calling for the sector's industrial development and modernization, as well as wider international reach. China has also continued to deepen health cooperation with countries around the world by promoting the use of artemisinin to benefit patients worldwide, regularly deploying medical teams abroad, establishing overseas traditional Chinese medicine centers, and joining efforts to combat Ebola. Through these efforts, it has worked with other countries to address cross-border public health risks. Yet as China's economy and society evolve and its demographic landscape changes, people's healthcare needs are becoming increasingly multi-layered and diverse. "At present and for a period to come, China's health and healthcare work needs to adapt to changing circumstances and refine certain specific policies and measures. However, the path of health and healthcare development with Chinese characteristics must not waver," Xi said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.
